small_guidance:
- The conv (nn.Conv2d on 128×8×256×256 → 32 out, k=3) almost certainly dominates the 7.14 ms; the post-conv fused kernel is already close to memory-bound optimal. Focus tuning effort on the conv path: try `torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = True` in `__init__` and ensure `channels_last` memory format on input/weight to hit better cuDNN kernels.
- For the fused kernel, since CPG=4 and HW=64516, try larger BLOCK (16384) with num_warps=8 and num_stages=3, and consider collapsing the two static channel loops by tiling `(CPG, BLOCK)` jointly so bias/scale/gn params load once per program rather than per-pass.
- Cache the sigmoid output of pass-1 in shared memory / registers to skip recomputation in pass-2 when HW fits — currently sigmoid is computed twice; a single-pass Welford with a final write loop avoids redundant exp().
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.Conv2d` with a custom Triton conv kernel fused with bias-add, scale, sigmoid, and GroupNorm stat accumulation. With in_channels=8, kernel=3×3, the K-dim of the implicit GEMM is only 72 — a direct conv (program per (N, OC-tile, output-tile)) loading the 3×3×8 weight into registers will outperform cuDNN at this small IC.
- Fuse the conv epilogue into the GroupNorm first pass: each conv program writes its tile and atomically (or via a second kernel reading the conv output) contributes partial sum/sumsq per group. With G=8, CPG=4, atomically accumulating 2 floats per (N, group) is cheap. Then a second small kernel finalizes mean/rstd and applies the affine in-place.
- Use channels_last (NHWC) layout end-to-end so the C dimension is contiguous — this lets the conv kernel issue 8-wide vector loads on input and 32-wide stores on output, and lets GN reductions coalesce across channel-groups.
